acceptance_criteria.statement: Pre-acquisition authorization fails closed; temporary execution denial preserves exact approved provenance, while material capability/binding/policy/reference mismatch durably stales and invalidates old approval.
Logical execution identity and canonical-json-v1 fingerprint are server-owned, caller-noninfluenceable, immutable and acquired atomically by exactly one contender.
Admission reloads current Workspace/resource/execution authority, compatibility and complete m4r1 integrity/trust/key state under the fixed epoch lock protocol.
Fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time commits one complete immutable DispatchAdmissionWitness; commit/ack ambiguity resolves to exact committed readback or complete rollback absence.
Admission is logical write start; later mutation or expiry cannot cancel, upgrade or retarget the original byte-identical envelope.
Independent SQLite provider atomically owns effects/closed outcomes and exact logical-ID/fingerprint idempotency, replay, conflict, cross-binding rejection and restart semantics.
Every post-admission uncertainty branch has exact provider state and remains Knora executing/indeterminate with unchanged identities and no #77 recovery authority.
Generation-1 observation/finalization uses fresh post-lock database time and expired owners cannot append observation/audit or terminal state.
Only named direct outcomes finalize; every execution outcome and every post-acquisition denial exactly matches a complete independently sourced sanitized application/HTTP matrix.
Restarted append-only audit reconstructs complete provenance while SQLite remains independent and all private/secret fields are absent; M1-M3 regressions stay green.

design_decisions.decision: Keep WriteProposalWorkflow.handle as the sole deep application Interface; witnesses and protocol ordering remain private.
Commit durable PostgreSQL admission before provider I/O and classify post-admission uncertainty as receipt-possible.
Persist the exact canonical envelope bytes with retained verification material and never regenerate after admission.
Use a private non-runtime trusted signing harness for provider defensive conflict and cross-binding coverage; prove it is unresolved by every production application/HTTP DI surface.
Persist read-only NoAdmission or AdmissionOutstanding recovery seeds; all runtime reconciliation/retry/takeover remains #78.
Use fresh PostgreSQL clock_timestamp after blocking locks for execution decisions.

invariants: No gateway call exists without one durable admission; at most one admission exists per logical execution.
Every acquisition loser and every denied admission row makes zero provider calls.
Every admission linearizes current authority, exact compatibility and complete m4r1 verification under fixed epochs.
Admission-first dispatch remains byte-identical despite later mutation or expiry.
Provider effects and idempotency outcomes commit atomically in provider-owned SQLite.
Provider scope/cross-binding rejection occurs before target lookup and before SQLite ledger/effect mutation.
Provider outcome not-found and named terminal rejection are disjoint typed states.
Issue #77 creates and acts only on generation 1 with no reconciliation, retry, replay authorization or takeover.
The capability registry remains static and typed with no plugin framework.
Test-only trusted signers and mutators cannot be resolved or invoked from production application/HTTP composition.
Every post-acquisition denial and every repeated-execute/execution outcome matches its immutable independently sourced application/HTTP matrix; every other field is forbidden.
Raw provider/routing, envelope/MAC, fingerprint, authority, key, credential and secret fields never enter public projections.
out_of_scope: ReconcileExecution, provider-first application recovery, stale takeover, generation 2+ and authorized replay, owned by #78.
Distributed rollback/cancellation or arbitrary remote-vendor time protocols.
Dynamic plugins, provider discovery or runtime registration.
Editing immutable proposals or reusing approval after material incompatibility.
Final M4 code review before Issues #75-#79 are accepted, integrated and closed.

test_cases.statement: Load an independent literal fixture with one physical row for missing/invalid authentication; malformed/non-object JSON; missing or non-integer/bool revision; both forbidden identity fields; path/current Workspace, resource and every limited execution-authority denial; capability/binding/policy identity/version/digest mismatch; every named m4r1 syntax/trust/key/expiry denial; and proposal expiry. Exercise each application-representable and exact HTTP row with direct durable before/after snapshots, named sentinels and old-approval retry where applicable.
test_cases.oracle: Every row has the exact independent application/transport outcome and closed HTTP status/body containing only error.code; no execution/acquisition/admission/execution-start or terminal-audit artifact and no gateway/target-lookup/provider call occurs. Authentication/path/validation rows also have zero proposal lookups and workflow calls. Temporary authority and m4r1 trust denials preserve exact approved provenance without granting reference reuse after malformed, mismatched, revoked or expired state; material mismatch durably stales/invalidates with a typed reason; proposal expiry preserves approval provenance while projecting approved, non-stale, non-executable and expired.

test_cases.statement: Reject caller identity injection, independently recompute canonical fingerprint across every boundary, race identified contenders and fault each acquisition write before commit/restart.
test_cases.oracle: Identities are server-owned and immutable; one complete AcquireApplied tuple commits, every loser has zero calls, pre-commit state is invisible and rollback leaves no fragment.

test_cases.statement: Block after acquisition; run every authority/selector/reference/trusted-store/key denial row plus compatible and transition controls, independently seed and durably reload expected proposal/acquisition identities before invocation, then compare private denial, ProposalNotExecutable projection and decoded HTTP status/body with an independently loaded exact matrix.
test_cases.oracle: Every denial occurs after post-lock reload, has exact application fields/reason and exact 400/403/409 closed error envelope, binds canonical IDs exactly equal to pre-invocation independently seeded/directly reloaded durable identities, persists zero admission/audit and makes zero gateway/provider calls; compatible controls admit once and transitions obey epoch linearization.

test_cases.statement: Race real epoch mutations and same-generation issuers; block acquisition/admission across proposal/reference/lease expiry under skewed non-database clocks.
test_cases.oracle: Mutation-first denies, admission-first binds prior epochs, one admission exists and fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time decides every expiry.

test_cases.statement: Compare the complete admission tuple/bytes, restart and rotate current key, then force committed-before-ack and rolled-back PostgreSQL branches with authoritative readback.
test_cases.oracle: Committed state equals intended bytes with no second insert/sign/regeneration; rollback has complete absence, zero call/retry and no partial third state.

test_cases.statement: Pause after admission, mutate/revoke every authority/selector/key and cross every expiry before dispatch resumes.
test_cases.oracle: Exactly one call carries the original byte-identical envelope/intent without reauthorization, cancellation, upgrade or retargeting.

test_cases.statement: At the private SQLite provider harness, cover replay, valid unequal fingerprints, ordinary tampering, independently valid cross-binding, success, three closed rejections, pre-commit rollback and committed-before-ack restart. For unequal-fingerprint conflict, seal a sanitized content-addressed correlation record with logical execution ID, attempted fingerprint/admission digests, existing SQLite row-set digest, typed result, lookup/effect counts and post-restart digest.
test_cases.oracle: Cross-binding returns provider_scope_denied after integrity verification but before target lookup and any SQLite ledger/effect mutation with exact zero counters. Conflict evidence proves one original ledger/effect, no second effect and stable provider truth after restart, but neither asserts nor authorizes Knora finalization; other rows preserve atomic effect/outcome, tamper and restart semantics.

test_cases.statement: Run admission-before-gateway, pre-SQLite-commit and committed-before-ack as named branches with success/rejection variants and read-only provider observation.
test_cases.oracle: First two are exact zero/zero, committed is exact one durable outcome, and every unfinalized branch stays executing/indeterminate with unchanged identities and no #77 recovery authority.

test_cases.statement: Restart/reload NoAdmission and AdmissionOutstanding seeds and call ExecuteApprovedProposal again.
test_cases.oracle: Both return the immutable-matrix ExecutionInProgress result with no provider observation, admission creation/replacement, dispatch/replay, retry, takeover or generation increment.

test_cases.statement: For provider success and every closed rejection, run observation and finalization independently: begin before the lease deadline, block on the governing execution-row lock, cross expiry under skewed non-database clocks, capture the operation's fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time and compare expired/before-expiry controls. Exercise every execution outcome and TC-03 denial through two independently loaded matrices; for ExecutionIndeterminate, both ExecutionInProgress rows, ExecutionFenced and every ProposalNotExecutable row, capture before-result, after-result and post-PostgreSQL-restart execution/finalization/terminal-audit snapshots, linking provider conflict to TC-07.
test_cases.oracle: Expired observation and finalization each prove start/transaction time before expiry but deciding post-lock clock_timestamp after expiry, return fenced and append zero operation-correlated writes; before-expiry controls use post-lock database time before the deadline and are not fenced. Every non-finalizing row remains generation 1 and executing after restart with unchanged proposal/logical-execution/fingerprint/admission identities, zero terminal outcome/finalization rows, zero terminal-audit append delta, zero operation-correlated finalization writes and unchanged terminal digest. Provider conflict retains the exact five-field ExecutionInProgress application/HTTP-409 projection and one original provider effect; every denial has exact independently sourced fields/identities and no row is unclassified.

test_cases.statement: Restart PostgreSQL and SQLite independently, reconstruct audit solely from append-only rows, read provider truth separately and scan forbidden fields.
test_cases.oracle: Complete provenance matches field-for-field, provider ledger stays independent and no raw/private/secret value leaks.

test_cases.statement: Inventory every production application/HTTP DI surface; probe resolution and invocation of every test-only signer/mutator plus registration/discovery/plugin loading, then run focused/full pytest serially, Ruff, Compose and clean Alembic verification.
test_cases.oracle: No production surface resolves a test-only adapter or dynamic seam and all probes leave dependency, registry, PostgreSQL, SQLite, lookup, provider and effect state unchanged; all verification remains green.

command_projections.statement: Clean PostgreSQL recreation and Alembic upgrade/current using pinned Python and serialized database.
Locked focused Issue #77 pytest files followed by full test and eval pytest suites.
Ruff, Docker Compose config, subject SHA, evidence bundle and clean-worktree verification.

required_evidence.statement: Independent literal pre-acquisition matrix/digest with one release row per authentication, validation, authorization, m4r1 trust/key/expiry and material-mismatch variant; exact application/HTTP envelopes and key sets; durable proposal/approval before-after snapshots and old-approval retry; named workflow/proposal-lookup/acquisition/admission/audit/gateway/target-lookup/provider sentinel identities and exact zero counts; plus identity-injection rejection, canonical recomputation and contender-correlated acquisition evidence.

Independently sourced complete post-acquisition private/application/HTTP denial matrix, per-row durable identity source references and expected/actual proposal/logical-execution identity equality, compatible/transition controls, all epoch/m4r1 traces, per-row zero admission/audit/gateway/provider counters and fresh PostgreSQL time samples.
Complete admission witness, exact envelope, ambiguity branches and admission-first non-cancellation evidence.

Provider-owned effect/outcome/replay/conflict/tamper/cross-binding/rollback/restart evidence, including cross-binding verification order and zero target-lookup/ledger/effect counters plus one sanitized content-addressed provider-conflict correlation record containing logical execution ID, attempted fingerprint/admission digests, existing SQLite row-set digest, typed conflict result, target-lookup/effect counts and post-restart digest.
Three exact crash-window records, provider-not-found distinction, two recovery seeds and absence of #78 behavior.

Independent observation/finalization clock tuples with operation start, transaction time, lock/crossing order, skewed non-database clocks, deciding post-lock clock_timestamp, before-expiry controls and operation-correlated state/write counts; for every non-finalizing matrix row, before/after/post-PostgreSQL-restart generation/lifecycle/identity snapshots, zero terminal outcome/finalization rows, zero terminal-audit delta, zero operation-correlated finalization writes and unchanged terminal digest, with provider conflict linked to EV-04; independent immutable execution-outcome and post-acquisition-denial matrices with per-row identity/HTTP/application comparisons; forbidden-field scans, production DI isolation, full audit reconstruction and governed verification identities/totals.

prior_findings.resolution: TC-03 retains the complete active/retiring/revoked/unknown/unavailable and rotation-transition key matrix with post-lock key identity/epoch and per-row counters.
TC-10 retains exact expired-owner observation/audit identity, count, digest and zero-write fencing evidence.
TC-12 retains production-composition closed-registry and structural no-registration/discovery/plugin probes.
TC-03 assigns every authority/selector/integrity/trusted-store row an exact typed result plus zero admission/audit/gateway/provider counters and a compatible control.
TC-07 treats cross-binding independently and requires provider_scope_denied before target lookup and SQLite ledger/effect mutation with exact zero counters.

TC-12 inventories every production application/HTTP DI surface and attempts both role/type resolution and invocation for every test-only trusted signer/mutator, requiring no returned object and zero state/provider change.

TC-03 and TC-10 retain the complete ProposalNotExecutable application/HTTP denial matrix and now bind proposal_id/logical_execution_id to canonical pre-invocation independently seeded/directly reloaded durable scenario identities with expected/actual equality evidence.

TC-10 independently races observation and finalization: each begins before lease expiry, blocks on the governing row lock, crosses expiry, captures the operation's deciding post-lock clock_timestamp and compares same-path before-expiry controls under skewed non-database clocks.

TC-01 now owns one independent literal pre-acquisition fixture row for every authentication, validation, authorization, material-mismatch, m4r1 trust/key/expiry and proposal-expiry variant, with exact application/HTTP envelopes, durable state, named zero-activity sentinels and one release-evidence row each.

TC-07 seals provider-conflict correlation evidence and TC-10 proves after PostgreSQL restart that provider conflict and every non-finalizing matrix row remain generation-1 executing with unchanged identities and zero terminal/finalization rows, terminal-audit appends or finalization writes.
